Abstract

SYNTHETIC TEST FIXTURE — not real data. Tibial loading improved recovery after brain injury in mice.

Introduction

Bone is an endocrine organ that signals to distant tissues.

Results

Tibial loading improves motor function after TBI. DCTAL improved pole test performance in TBI mice (n = 12 mice per group; Fig. 1b). DCTAL increased serum Hsp70 levels in TBI mice (Fig. 1c).

Osteocyte Piezo1 is required for the benefit. DCTAL ameliorated motor and cognitive deficits in TBI-Piezo1fl/fl mice, but not in TBI-Piezo1Sost-Cre/ERT2 mice (Fig. 2d-h). Two mice were excluded from the analysis because of surgical complications.

Hsp70 protects neurons. Recombinant Hsp70 reduced neuronal loss in TBI mice (Fig. 3a).

Methods

Tibial loading. Mice received dynamic compressive loading of the tibia at 2 Hz for 1,200 cycles per session. No animals were excluded from the analyses.

Statistics. Data are mean ± s.e.m.

Fig. 1 | Tibial loading improves recovery. b, Pole test after DCTAL, n = 10 mice per group. c, Serum Hsp70, n = 8 mice. Loading was applied at 4 Hz.

Fig. 2 | Piezo1 deletion in osteocytes abolishes the effect. d-h, n = 14, 14, 14 and 17 mice.

Fig. 3 | Hsp70 is neuroprotective. a, NeuN+ cell counts, n = 6 mice.
